head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: Scope: all 34 manifest files read in full; no partners; no files removed from scope (SEC-004). Known-ledger security/correctness entries on policy.go/git.go (lifetime=task exemption, git rm --cached, tag-shadowed base ref, rename detection, branch-chosen base_ref, non -z path parsing) were not re-reported. Unpromoted suspicions, for the station: (1) cross-chunk, unverified: validateScopeName (internal/sessions/sessions.go:223-230) admits names like '.. ' (trailing space) and '...'; on Windows, Win32 path normalization strips trailing spaces/dots from components, so DeleteScope('.. ') could resolve sessions\archived\.. -> sessions\ and RemoveAll the whole sessions dir. Not demonstrable here (darwin host, Windows normalization of a '..'-plus-space component unconfirmed) and reachability depends on the config-server HTTP handlers in another chunk — escalate for a Windows probe rather than treat as a finding. (2) cmd/configserver/main.go startPeek's /healthz identity match (claudeHome/codexHome strings) is spoofable by any local user who binds 127.0.0.1:<peek-port> first; not a regression (the previous code reused any listener) and only matters on multi-user hosts, so not raised. (3) ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-003 curl probes: none apply — the changed surfaces in this chunk are a CLI gate and library code, no HTTP endpoint changed here.

findings.claim: CheckPolicy's frozen surface (policySurface, policy.go:31-36) covers only the four acdsl/*.json files and ruleDelta only declaration-marker files, so the verifier implementations the base registry binds are freely editable off the base branch: in a gated/strict repo a branch rewrites the verifier a protected rule runs (bin/verifiers/<name> in a dist target, the script a sanctioned registry.local.json entry points at, or cmd/acdsl/verifiers/<name> in a source repo) to exit 0, every rule bound to it passes, and CheckPolicy reports nothing — contradicting the check contract in cmd/acdsl/main.go:13-14 ('strict/gated repos may not change rules or verifiers off the base branch').
findings.exploit: Quantified: 1 attempt, one file write, under a minute, no privilege beyond write access to the branch worktree. Sequence in a dist target (dist_mode=gated ships mode gated via writePolicy, dist.go:243-245): on an agent branch run `printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > bin/verifiers/gofmt` (registry.json argv rewritten to bin/verifiers/gofmt by writeDistRegistry, dist.go:206-208), then `./bin/acdsl check` -> CheckPolicy: surfaceDelta compares only acdsl/policy.json, policy.schema.json, registry.json, evalgen.json (all unchanged) -> 0 diagnostics; overlayViolations -> no overlay -> 0; ruleDelta -> no declaration file changed -> empty delta; Check then runs the replaced verifier -> exit 0 for every gofmt-bound rule (ACDSL-GOLANG-FMT-001 etc.) -> 'acdsl: N rule(s) OK'. Same outcome with a sanctioned overlay entry (local_overrides) whose argv script is edited, which the base policy cannot pin either. No curl probe applies (CLI gate, not an HTTP surface); reproduction is the two commands above.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go in full: policySurface (31-36) lists exactly four JSON paths; surfaceDelta (300-321) iterates only that list; ruleDelta (237-280) keeps only paths for which declarationMarker reports a declaration; overlayViolations (143-173) checks overlay entry NAMES against local_overrides, never their argv targets; CheckPolicy (329-376) composes only these three. Re-read dist.go 198-261: shipped registry argv is rewritten to bin/verifiers/<name> and the source dist_mode (gated in the committed acdsl/policy.json) becomes the target mode. run.go:110-116 executes entry.Argv[0] from root, so the file at that path is what decides the verdict. cmd/acdsl/main.go:122-137 runs CheckPolicy then Check with no other verifier integrity step. Not a variant of a known entry: known security-MAJ-1-r2 (lifetime=task exemption), security-MAJ-9-r1 (git rm --cached declaration file), security-MIN-11-r1 (tag shadowing base ref), security-MAJ-2-r1 (rename detection) and correctness-MAJ-9-r1 (branch-chosen base_ref) all attack rule/base resolution, none the verifier implementation. Caveat stated honestly: bin/acdsl itself is equally branch-local, so a complete fix also needs the runner pinned; the verifier half is still an independent, documented promise that fails.
findings.fix: Pin verifier artifacts on the base: add an optional verifier_digests map (name -> sha256 of the argv[0] file, or of the go-run package dir for source repos) to the base policy, written by dist/writePolicy, and have CheckPolicy diagnose any registry-bound verifier (base registry plus sanctioned overlay entries) whose working-tree digest differs from the base policy's.
